query: When does private defence start and when does it end?

gold_references.label: Section 40
gold_references.role: commencement and continuance of right of private defence of body

gold_references.label: Section 43
gold_references.role: commencement and continuance of right of private defence of property

acceptable_references.label: Section 37
acceptable_references.reason: restrictions on private defence including when public authority can be approached

required_points: Section 40 provides that the right of private defence of body commences as soon as a reasonable apprehension of danger to the body arises from an attempt or threat to commit the offence, even though the offence may not have been committed; and continues as long as the apprehension of danger continues.

Section 43 provides that the right of private defence of property commences when a reasonable apprehension of danger to the property commences; and continues in different ways depending on whether the threat is theft, robbery, or trespass.
optional_points: The right ends when the apprehension of danger ends or when public authority assistance becomes available.
forbidden_points: Private defence can only start after the first blow is struck.
Private defence continues indefinitely after an attack.

notes: Multi-hop query requiring both Section 40 and Section 43.
